hero.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
hero.teaser: Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton.
hero.body:
Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized.

 The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay. Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete.

 Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, said Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab. With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine, the district was able to add these on.

 The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out. The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027.

cards.teaser: A child died and another was hospitalized after a bicycle collided with a FedEx truck Monday afternoon on East Midway Road in Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
A child is dead and another is hospitalized after a bicycle collided with a FedEx truck Monday afternoon in Fort Pierce, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash happened around 3:07 p.m. in the 600 block of East Midway Road. Two juveniles riding a bicycle collided with a FedEx truck, and one child was pronounced dead at the scene. The second child was taken to a hospital in stable condition.

Megan Sharma, who lives near the scene, told WPTV that the area is commonly used by people on bikes. She said kids go up and down the sidewalk all the time on both sides of the road and called the incident tragic and horrible. Sharma also said tragedy took place along East Midway Road in 2020 when a young adult on a motorcycle was hit by a car. She described the road as a dangerous highway.

cards.headline: Family files wrongful death lawsuit after girl killed in go-kart crash at Port St. Lucie Urban Air Adventure Park
cards.teaser: The family of 6-year-old Emma Riddle filed a wrongful death lawsuit against Urban Air Trampoline and Adventure Park after she died in a go-kart crash at the Port St. Lucie facility in December 2025.
cards.body:
Emma Riddle, 6, visited Urban Air Trampoline and Adventure Park in Port St. Lucie with her mother and sister in December 2023, where they rode electric go-karts. The child was seated with her mom in a double-seat go-kart while her older sister was in a single-rider go-kart. According to the complaint filed by Morgan & Morgan injury law firm, there were multiple alleged safety protocols ignored that allegedly led Emma's go-kart to accelerate to a high speed and crash into the track wall. Emma suffered severe injuries and was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she later died. The child's parents filed a wrongful death lawsuit Monday against the Port St. Lucie business, alleging that Urban Air created dangerous conditions that contributed to Emma's death.

The family claims the adventure park ignored safety rules and manufacturer guidelines. At 50 inches, Emma was nearly a foot shorter and twelve years younger than the manufacturer's minimum stated recommendations for operating a double-seat go-kart, and yet, she was permitted to ride, the lawsuit alleges. Earlier this year, documents showed the Florida Department of Agriculture reached a $300,000 settlement agreement with Urban Air Adventure Park following an investigation into the fatal incident. Morgan & Morgan founder John Morgan said Urban Air has a duty to protect every child that walks through their doors and the firm alleges they failed Emma in the most devastating way imaginable.

cards.headline: Martin County deputies rescue 80 cats from Stuart home in worst hoarding case sheriff has seen
cards.body:
Martin County deputies rescued dozens of cats Monday from a Stuart home that Sheriff John Budensiek described as the worst animal hoarding case he has seen in the county. The Martin County Sheriff's Office, Animal Control and Martin County Fire Rescue responded to a home in the 11500 block of Southwest Meadowlark Circle after an investigation into reports that a U.S. Postal Service employee had been collecting feral cats along her mail route.

Budensiek identified the homeowner as 77-year-old Gail Giustino. Investigators believe she was not stealing pets but was gathering feral cats and bringing them home. Authorities obtained a search warrant after Giustino allegedly refused to allow Animal Control officers inside the home during multiple attempts over the past week. When deputies entered the house Monday, they found what the sheriff described as horrific living conditions. The home had no working air conditioning, little to no ventilation and, in some areas, up to a foot of animal feces covering the floor. Budensiek said the odor was overwhelming, and Martin County Fire Rescue's Hazardous Materials Team had to ventilate the home before rescuers could safely enter.

Giustino told deputies she believed there were at least 70 cats inside the home, all kept in cages. Authorities believe there could ultimately be 70 to 80 animals or more, including several dogs, though an exact count had not been completed Monday evening. The rescued animals are being taken to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, which is expected to rely on foster families and volunteers to help care for them. Authorities said they are still evaluating the animals' medical conditions. Officials said Animal Control had previously cited Giustino dozens of times for animal-related violations about 10 years ago, but they believe she gradually returned to hoarding animals after complying with earlier code enforcement requirements.

Budensiek said Giustino was arrested on two misdemeanor animal cruelty-related charges, though investigators said they could have pursued significantly more charges. The sheriff said the criminal charges were filed primarily to obtain the search warrant, remove the animals from the home and prevent Giustino from acquiring additional animals while she seeks help through the mental health court system. "If we believe she was truly an animal abuser ... we would try to bury her under the jail," Budensiek said. "We truly believe that Gail thinks she's doing the right thing, but she's doing it the wrong way."

cards.headline: 85 percent of Florida families spend more than affordability benchmark on childcare, Fed report finds
cards.body:
The cost of childcare has become an affordability crisis for Florida families, with 85.4 percent spending more than the federal benchmark on care, according to a new report from the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta. The study found that from 2020 to 2024, childcare prices increased by 29 percent nationwide, compared with a 22 percent rise in overall prices during the same period.

The Atlanta Fed examined childcare costs in Georgia and Florida and found that childcare expenses now often far exceed the 7 percent of income affordability benchmark established by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. The estimated weekly costs for the care of infants and toddlers in Florida are $268, while preschool-aged children cost an estimated $208 per week. The median percentage of income families would need to pay for childcare is 13.9 percent.

According to the report, in Florida, the median percentage of income families would need to pay for childcare is 16.8 percent, more than double the federal standard. These costs are putting significant financial pressure on parents across the state and forcing difficult decisions about work hours. Some families are even leaving jobs due to the burden of childcare expenses.

The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta's research highlights a growing economic challenge for working families throughout Florida. The 29 percent increase in childcare prices over four years represents a steeper climb than general inflation, creating a widening gap between what families earn and what they must pay to keep children in care while parents work. The report is available in full from the Atlanta Fed.

cards.headline: Florida back-to-school tax holiday begins, runs through August 20
cards.teaser: Florida families can purchase school supplies, clothing, and electronics without paying sales tax during the month-long tax holiday that started Monday.
cards.body:
Florida's annual back-to-school sales tax holiday kicked off Monday, giving families statewide a chance to save money on school supplies, clothing and electronics ahead of the new school year. The tax-free period runs through Thursday, Aug. 20, allowing shoppers to purchase qualifying items without paying Florida's sales tax. The tax holiday covers clothing, footwear, and accessories priced at $100 or less per item, including shirts, pants, dresses, shoes, boots, and accessories like belts and hats. School supplies under $50 per item are tax-free, covering everything from notebooks and pencils to binders, markers, scissors, and lunch boxes. Learning aids and jigsaw puzzles priced at $30 or less are included, such as flashcards, educational toys, and puzzle books.

Personal computers and related accessories under $1,500 qualify for the tax exemption, including laptops, tablets, desktops, electronic book readers, and accessories like keyboards, mice, monitors, and routers. Cell phones, video game consoles, and recreational devices don't qualify. Wallets and bags under $100 per item are covered, including backpacks, handbags, and fanny packs, though briefcases and suitcases are excluded. The tax holiday doesn't apply to rentals or repairs of qualifying items, and purchases made at theme parks, entertainment complexes, hotels, or airports are excluded from the exemption. Governor Ron DeSantis signed the tax holiday into law as part of the state's effort to help families manage back-to-school expenses.

cards.headline: New tuition-free tech school opening in Fort Pierce in August
cards.teaser: SouthTech Treasure Coast will open in Fort Pierce in August, giving middle and high school students the opportunity to earn industry certifications while completing their traditional coursework.
cards.body:
A new tuition-free career and technical charter school is preparing to open in Fort Pierce in August. SouthTech Treasure Coast will give middle and high school students the opportunity to earn industry certifications while completing their traditional coursework. The St. Lucie County School Board approved the charter application for the Fort Pierce campus in April.

 School leaders say they selected the Treasure Coast because of the area's growing demand for skilled workers. The Fort Pierce campus will serve students in grades 6 through 12, with plans to enroll about 460 students in its first year.

 Students will have the opportunity to choose from career academies including medical science, culinary arts, cosmetology, and agriculture technology. Carla Lovett, Executive Director of SouthTech Schools, said all students are working on their academics, but they are also all in one of the career academies where they have the opportunity to earn adult level industry certifications while they are still in high school.

 SouthTech Treasure Coast will host a grand opening celebration on Saturday, July 25, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m., giving families and community members a chance to tour the new campus and learn more about the programs being offered. SouthTech Treasure Coast in Fort Pierce is located at 2810 S. US Highway 1 Fort Pierce, FL 34982.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County firefighters' union disputes hazing findings, calls terminations unjust
cards.teaser: The union representing St. Lucie County Fire District firefighters is pushing back against the termination of three firefighters and suspension of two others, calling the investigation biased.
cards.body:
Professional Firefighters and Paramedics of St. Lucie County, IAFF Local 1377, said the St. Lucie County Fire District wrongly terminated and suspended the five members for their involvement in incidents that occurred in March and September 2024. Local 1377 President Ryan Sapp stated in a letter obtained by WPTV that these incidents did not involve any hazing. Sapp pointed to the Fort Pierce Police Department's report, which he said described the situation, in part, as "found coworkers entertaining each other." The union's position is that all five were wrongly found to be in violation of fire district policies and disciplined without just cause.

 The union raised concerns about the outside law firm the fire district hired to conduct its investigation, Allen, Norton & Blue. Local 1377 and its legal counsel said the investigation was not conducted in an impartial or unbiased manner. Sapp stated in the letter that the nature of the questions asked, as well as the way in which they were asked or not asked, reflects a predetermined conclusion rather than an objective fact-finding process.

 Sapp noted that the same firm that conducted the investigation has since been hired by the fire district to represent it at arbitration. Local 1377 has demanded arbitration for all five members and said it remains willing to negotiate a reasonable resolution that would avoid the significant costs of arbitration and save both the taxpayers and the union a substantial amount of money.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County residents adjust diets as E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks spread
cards.teaser: Health officials confirmed five local cases of cyclospora since May, including two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County, prompting residents to change what they eat and avoid.
cards.body:
Concerns over contaminated produce linked to E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks are prompting South Florida residents to reconsider their food choices, with some avoiding leafy greens entirely. The outbreaks have affected thousands nationwide and include lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials have confirmed local cases stretching from the Palm Beaches to the Treasure Coast, including two cases in St. Lucie County.

 The Florida Department of Health reported five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May. Two cases were reported in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County, and one in Martin County. The contamination concerns have led families across the region to change their eating habits at restaurants, grocery stores, and fast-food chains.

 Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, who were visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are trying to stay away from lettuce and stuff like that. Other families are similarly steering clear of leafy greens altogether as reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country. The widespread nature of the outbreaks has left many consumers uncertain about which products are safe to purchase and consume.

 Samantha Barone, a dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, offered guidance for consumers looking to maintain healthy diets while avoiding potentially contaminated produce. Barone recommends sticking to melon and things that have a harder skin that you can peel. She advises consumers to focus on produce with protective outer layers and to wash all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them.

 For those seeking alternatives to leafy greens, Barone suggests that beans and nuts are safe options that still provide fiber and protein. She specifically recommends cleaning produce using a mixture of one part distilled white vinegar to three parts water. The outbreaks have highlighted the importance of proper food handling and preparation practices for consumers across South Florida.

cards.headline: Boynton Beach firefighters rescue dog from raw sewage lift station
cards.teaser: A dog fell roughly 10 to 12 feet into a lift station holding about 2 feet of raw sewage Thursday, prompting a specialized confined space rescue.
cards.body:
A dog fell roughly 10 to 12 feet into a lift station holding about 2 feet of raw sewage Thursday, prompting a specialized confined space rescue by Boynton Beach Fire Rescue Department. Squad 6 crews arrived and assessed the scene before upgrading the incident to a Special Operations confined space rescue, the department said. Firefighters developed a rescue plan and had Firefighter Ramirez properly rigged and ready to enter the lift station.

 From the time he went on air, Firefighter Ramirez rescued the dog and safely exited the lift station in just 4 minutes, the department said. Once above ground, crews decontaminated the dog and gave it oxygen before turning it over to Animal Control. Animal Control successfully reunited the dog with its owner, according to a Facebook post from the department.

cards.headline: Wellington teen injured after electric bike rider strikes him during stunt near Lion Country Safari
cards.teaser: A Wellington teenager suffered multiple injuries, including broken bones, after being struck by an electric bike rider performing a wheelie on Tuesday night.
cards.body:
Seventeen-year-old Chad Filer said he was riding his scooter along a relatively isolated stretch of road between the Deer Run community and Lion Country Safari on Tuesday night when three teenage boys on dirt and electric bikes approached him. According to Chad, one rider began performing a wheelie and intentionally swerved toward him in what he described as a common "bike life" stunt meant to intimidate people before pulling away at the last second, but instead the bike struck the right side of his body.

 Chad estimates the rider was traveling around 40 mph when the impact sent him to the ground. A driver stopped to help, and Chad said the riders initially stayed nearby and told him he was "fine," but once witnesses called 911, the group fled.

 Doctors found Chad suffered broken metatarsal bones, three broken toes, significant bruising and multiple road rash injuries across his chest, knee, elbow and side. His mother, Cortez Hornsby, said part of one nipple was partially detached in the crash. The family faces mounting medical expenses because Chad's health insurance through work was not scheduled to begin until next month.

 Hornsby says she called the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office and was told this is a county-wide problem. She also says deputies told her that based on how isolated the crash site is and the lack of cameras, it may be difficult to find the teens. Chad cannot work while he heals, and the scooter he relied on for transportation was heavily damaged.

cards.headline: Wildfire burns 2,500 acres in western Palm Beach County, 30% contained
cards.teaser: A wildfire burning in western Palm Beach County has grown to 2,500 acres and is 30% contained, according to the Florida Forest Service.
cards.body:
A wildfire burning in western Palm Beach County has grown to 2,500 acres and is 30% contained, according to the Florida Forest Service. The Berger Fire remains active in Palm Beach County within the Florida Forest Service's Everglades field unit. As of 3:02 p.m. Saturday, the Florida Forest Service reported the fire had burned approximately 2,500 acres.

 The wildfire comes as the region experienced severe weather Friday that left a trail of impacts across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Residents sent multiple videos to the WPTV newsroom from Sebastian showing a large waterspout passing over the Indian River Lagoon Friday afternoon. In Port St. Lucie, weather spotters captured video of heavy rain moving through the area, with one resident reporting her rain gauge caught over 3 inches.

 The severe weather stretched all the way to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. Port St. Lucie also saw significant lightning activity.

 The St. Lucie County Fire District said crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. Fire crews also responded to an evening house fire at the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue.

 While radar picked up significant lightning in the area at the time, the St. Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate.

 Merry Moore O'Rourke, a resident who experienced the storms in Port St. Lucie, described the intensity of the weather. "All of a sudden, it got black.

 The wind started just raging and the sky had lit up like I have not seen," Moore O'Rourke said. She summed up what many across the region felt as the storms moved through. "I mean it was radical.

 I mean it was it was a little scary," Moore O'Rourke said. From waterspouts to lightning strikes and fires, Friday's severe weather served as a reminder of nature's unpredictable power across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. The Berger Fire situation remains developing as officials continue containment efforts.

cards.headline: Second arrest made in fatal shooting of Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Leonard Barnes
cards.teaser: Dale A. Mincey, 41, Barnes' nephew, was formally charged with first-degree murder Saturday in connection with the July 7 shooting on the 2700 block of Essex Drive.
cards.body:
The fatal shooting happened July 7 at a residence on the 2700 block of Essex Drive. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle.

 Barnes was taken to a local hospital, where he died. Dale A. Mincey, 41, Barnes' nephew, was formally charged with first-degree murder Saturday in connection with Barnes' death.

 Mincey remains in custody at the St. Lucie County Jail and is being held without bond. During questioning, Mincey told detectives he could not recall what happened the day of the shooting and that he didn't have any issues with Barnes and did not know how Barnes died, an arrest affidavit said. However, he admitted to owning two firearms.

 Karen Moye, the victim's sister and mother of the suspect, was also at the home when the shooting occurred. She heard a loud bang while she was in the bathroom and came out to find Mincey and called police, an arrest affidavit said. Moye, who lived in the home with Mincey and Barnes, told detectives immediately after the shooting that the pair did not have a good relationship and that Mincey told her he was expressing fear in the days leading up to the shooting.

 Sheriff Richard Del Toro said Moye knowingly provided false information to investigators and withheld pertinent information related to this homicide investigation. She has been charged with false report to law enforcement and the commission of a capital felony. Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. Gaines Academy.

cards.body:
Deputies spotted 33-year-old Markell Tillman driving aggressively at speeds exceeding 100 mph on State Road 710, forcing other vehicles off the roadway. When deputies attempted to stop him, Tillman fled. Tillman weaved through traffic in an attempt to lose deputies before turning onto SW Martin Highway toward Palm City, where he continued to drive recklessly.

 Deputies spotted Tillman again traveling eastbound on Martin Highway near Allapattah Road. Deputies used stop sticks to disable his vehicle near I-95. Tillman then bailed out of the vehicle and attempted to flee on foot before deputies caught up with him and took him into custody.

 Tillman was arrested on charges including fleeing and eluding, aggravated fleeing with injury or damage, operating a vehicle exceeding the speed limit by 50 or more mph, driving while license suspended or revoked, obstruction without violence, and operating a vehicle at 100 or more mph. Tillman also had an out-of-county warrant at the time of his arrest. He was booked into the Martin County Jail.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound couple seeks community support as husband battles head and neck cancer
hero.teaser: A Hobe Sound couple is asking for community support as they navigate a cancer diagnosis, holding onto faith every step of the way.
hero.body:
Dave and Faren Motz met in South Florida before moving to Maui, where they married and raised their family. Faren raised all three of their kids and home schooled. The couple started a business and had a farm where they served children.

 Years later, they moved to Hobe Sound and purchased a property, but just months after settling in, Dave was diagnosed with head and neck cancer. As the couple searched for the right healthcare in Florida, AdventHealth in Celebration provided programs and grants that became a critical resource.

 Dave underwent nearly seven weeks of daily radiation treatments. The repeated visits to Orlando, biopsies, scans, and exams added up, costing the couple nearly $20,000 out of pocket. Their age and income kept them from qualifying for Medicare or Medicaid.

 Dave, a former firefighter, had long been the family's provider. Now, Faren has stepped up to support them both, driving him back and forth from Orlando for treatment. Doctors told Dave he has an 85% chance of recovery.

 Faren works at Latitudes at the Jupiter Beach Resort, where those who want to show their support can stop by and visit. Those who would like to contribute financially can donate to the family's GoFundMe at Standing with Dave Motz in his cancer battle.

cards.headline: Some Villa Del Sol residents return home nearly 2 years after structural damage forced evacuation
cards.teaser: Villa Del Sol residents in St. Lucie County told WPTV they are able to return home after nearly two years of being displaced from their condos following structural damage found in August 2024.
cards.body:
Residents told WPTV they were notified last month they could return to their condos, after an inspection in August 2024 found structural damage in buildings 3, 4, and 5, which were deemed unsafe. Katie Johnson was the first to share to WPTV that residents had been told they could come back. WPTV received emails sent to residents from the Board of Directors telling them they could return.

 WPTV also obtained a letter from engineers sent to St. Lucie County's Building Department requesting they lift occupancy restrictions following their special inspection. Katie Johnson described the work still underway at the property, saying they're still moving the dirt back under the buildings.

 Robert Segedin took WPTV inside his family's home, excited to return but thinking about those who cannot. Eric Johnson is among those not coming back. He was one of the first residents WPTV met at Villa Del Sol and is now living in Georgia.

 Eric Johnson said the financial toll has been severe, explaining the family had to drain out all their savings accounts and all their 401ks just trying to make ends meet while this was going on. He is filing for bankruptcy and filing his condo for foreclosure. Katie Johnson said she is thinking of neighbors like Eric Johnson who cannot return, saying she feels so bad that some were hit harder than others with the situation.

cards.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK route in September, citing low demand
cards.teaser: JetBlue is ending its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport on Sept. 9, just nine months after the route launched in December.
cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. Dambeck said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates, with air carriers fluctuating based off of demand.

 Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time if the airline had stayed with it. Ahern said the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach is hard to beat because it is easy and close. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

 Dambeck said JetBlue will evaluate continuously, so just because the route is gone now does not mean it will never come back. The Boston route from Vero Beach is seeing great demand, Dambeck said.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie couple fights rezoning of lot behind their home, says voices went unheard
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie couple is searching for answers after the city council voted to rezone the lot behind their home from residential to commercial, despite their months-long opposition.
cards.body:
The Mucciolos have called Port St. Lucie home for years, drawn to the property by its beautiful setting and backyard views of nature. In a unanimous vote, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved changing the lot behind their yard, where trees currently stand, to be rezoned from residential to commercial. The council says the change is necessary to reduce traffic in the neighborhood.

 One council member said adding commercial closer to neighborhoods reduces the length of trips, which reduces overall traffic because shorter trips reduce the burden on the overall network. Joseph Mucciolo said the trees will be gone in six months or a year.

 The two spoke at Monday's meeting, voicing their concerns, but they feel the council left them unheard. The council held its second reading Monday. While there was public comment, it was what's called a quasi-judicial hearing, meaning council members act as a panel of judges, applying existing zoning rules to a specific property and making decisions based strictly on sworn testimony and factual evidence, not public opinion.

 Joseph Mucciolo said the couple fought for months and feels their voices have gone unheard except for the news media. The Mucciolos say they will be exploring any kind of appeal process to change this outcome or to change the next one. Margaret Mucciolo said the process needs to change until it's logical, transparent, caring, and provides hope for people.

cards.headline: E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks hit Treasure Coast, residents avoid lettuce and berries
cards.teaser: Two confirmed cases of cyclospora infections occurred in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County since May, part of nationwide E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks linked to contamin
cards.body:
Two confirmed cases of cyclospora infections occurred in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County since May, part of nationwide E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks linked to contaminated lettuce, according to the Florida Department of Health. Palm Beach County reported two additional cases. Thousands across the United States have been affected by the outbreaks, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations.

 Residents across South Florida are changing their diets in response to the health threat. Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are staying away from lettuce. Jenny Rhodes said she misses salads and berries but prefers being careful.

 George Lorenz said he heard about the outbreak and is avoiding contaminated foods while eating pizza in downtown West Palm Beach on Clematis Street with his father Brian. Hendriette Peckens in Boynton Beach bought two big bags of oranges, bread and apples instead of produce and planned to cook Alaskan salmon for dinner.

 Samantha Barone, a dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should focus on produce with protective outer layers like melons, bananas and avocados. She said people should stick to melon and things with harder skin that can be peeled, but emphasized the importance of washing them before cutting and peeling. Barone recommended washing all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them and said beans and nuts are safe alternatives that provide fiber and protein.

 She warned against bagged lettuce and recommended buying whole heads of lettuce and peeling away the outer layers. She also advised avoiding berries, especially raspberries, because they are difficult to clean properly. Brian Lorenz said he is not avoiding anything but is washing all food.

 Barone recommended cleaning produce using a one to three part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water, then soaking, massaging and cleaning off produce before cooking vegetables. The outbreaks stem from contaminated produce that can cause severe stomach illness and intense diarrhea. Barone emphasized that the outbreaks are not an excuse to abandon healthy eating, telling people not to say to heck with fruits and vegetables and hit the donuts. She said consumers still want to remain healthy despite the contamination concerns affecting produce typically considered healthier options.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce neighbors pack planning meeting over Causeway Cove high-rise development proposal
cards.teaser: The Causeway Cove development project was reviewed by the Fort Pierce Planning Board on Monday. The project includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall.
cards.body:
The Causeway Cove development project was reviewed by the Fort Pierce Planning Board on Monday. The project, located off Seaway Drive, includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall, more than four times the city's height limit. Plans also call for two hotels and more than 70,000 square feet of retail space.

 The development qualifies under the Live Local Act, a state law passed in 2023 that allows developers to bypass height and density restrictions as long as they set aside 40% of units for affordable housing for at least 30 years. The project includes more than 900 apartments and condos, with 365 of those designated as affordable housing.

 Neighbors packed the chamber during the Monday meeting. Buster Brewster, a boater at Causeway Cove Marina, said he worries the project will change the character of the area. Dennis Fein raised concerns about traffic, saying nobody has thought this out and predicting massive traffic jams with nobody able to get on or off the island.

 City Planning Director Kev Freeman said developers must add traffic mitigation efforts and any required intersection or access improvements. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the city has no authority over whether the project is approved, stating the city does not have a play here and this is regulated by the state of Florida in the entirety. City commissioners are scheduled to hear a review of the project as the next step in the process.

cards.headline: Humane Society of the Treasure Coast seeks fosters and adopters during shelter renovation
cards.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation.
cards.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation. The construction will modernize the shelter, improve animal living spaces, enhance adoption areas, and create more comfortable and visible spaces to care for animals. In the meantime, the renovation presents significant challenges for the animals, who are being held in smaller spaces during the work.

 Sarah Fisher of the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast said these animals are really being affected by the sound of the construction. It's very, very loud and the sound being in a closed kennel can be very stressful for an animal. About 50 animals are currently in foster care, but the shelter is hoping to get the remaining 67 animals housed on-site either fostered or adopted, with most of them being dogs. The shelter continues to receive animals daily and is on a mission to get them out as quickly as they come in.

hero.headline: Messi bathed Yamal as baby in 2007 photo shoot, now they meet in World Cup final
hero.teaser: A 2007 charity calendar photo shoot paired teenage Lionel Messi with infant Lamine Yamal. Now 19 years later, they face off in Sunday's World Cup final.
hero.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for The Associated Press, took the photos after Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró near Barcelona who wanted to participate.

 Soccer destiny paired her baby boy with the Argentine who would become the greatest of all time. Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble. Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

 Monfort had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal led Spain to the title. The photo went viral then, but interest has skyrocketed with Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain approaching. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without any credit or compensation.

 The 19-year-old Yamal will face a Messi who is 20 years his senior in Sunday's final. Monfort, 58, is considering traveling to see the final in New Jersey. He said his heart is split and he does not know if he wants Messi or Yamal to win.

cards.headline: President Trump to Attend World Cup Final in New Jersey with Stepped-Up Security
cards.teaser: The World Cup final Sunday in New Jersey has been designated a Level 1 Special Event with President Trump attending the trophy presentation and enhanced security from multiple federal agencies.
cards.body:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup began with 48 teams playing over 39 days. Now it comes down to one final match Sunday in New Jersey. As Argentina and Spain prepare to take the pitch, a sprawling network of federal agents, local law enforcement, and private companies continue with a game plan two years in the making to ensure the final is safe.

 A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament.

 The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. When Trump attended an NBA Finals game last month in New York, police shut down several city blocks around the arena and fans were forced to wait in extra-long lines to go through enhanced security.

 The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle.

cards.headline: Major League Baseball Restricts iPad Use in Dugouts to Block AI Decision-Making
cards.teaser: MLB has made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible starting Wednesday to prevent teams from using artificial intelligence to make in-game decisions about substitutions and pitch calling.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball is restricting iPad usage in dugouts to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs. MLB made the custom tabs inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night, when the second half of the season started.

 MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators that in many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches. The memo was first reported by The Athletic and was obtained by The Associated Press.

 A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Sword wrote that instituting this prohibition beginning with the second half of the season is intended to provide clubs that have relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead-time to make any necessary adjustments. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Britain's Josh Kerr breaks mile world record with 3:42.66 run in London
cards.teaser: Josh Kerr shattered a 27-year-old world record on Saturday, running the mile in 3:42.66 at a Diamond League event in London.
cards.body:
Great Britain's Josh Kerr ran the mile in 3:42.66 on Saturday in London, breaking Hicham El Guerrouj's previous mark of 3:43.13 set in 1999. The 27-year-old made no secret that he was targeting the long-standing record at Saturday's Diamond League event in London. Earlier this week, he revealed he ran 2:42.45 in a 1,200-meter time trial.

 His sponsor, Brooks, dubbed the effort "Project 222," referencing the number of seconds in 3 minutes, 42 seconds. American Yared Nuguse finished second in 3:45.69.

 Kerr has emerged as one of the world's top middle-distance runners, winning bronze in the 1,500 meters at the Tokyo Olympics and silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Before turning professional, Kerr starred at the University of New Mexico, where he won multiple NCAA titles. He also set an NCAA indoor mile record of 3:35.01 in 2018. Kerr's record-setting run came during the Diamond League, an established international circuit of professional track and field events.

cards.headline: Spain defeats Argentina 1-0 to win 2026 World Cup in extra time thriller
cards.teaser: Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 on Sunday to win the 2026 FIFA World Cup championship. Ferran Torres scored the winning goal in the 106th minute of extra time, burying a left-footed s
cards.body:
Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 on Sunday to win the 2026 FIFA World Cup championship. Ferran Torres scored the winning goal in the 106th minute of extra time, burying a left-footed shot just under the crossbar after pouncing on a bouncing ball in the box. It is Spain's second World Cup championship and first since 2010.

 Spain was absolutely dominant throughout the match in terms of possession and shot attempts. The team took 15 shots in regulation while Argentina managed none. Spain also won nine corners compared to Argentina's single corner kick.

 Despite this overwhelming advantage, Lionel Messi and Argentina found a way to hang on and force the match into extra time. Torres broke through in the opening moment of the second 15-minute period of extra time to finally secure the victory for Spain.

 Argentina's task became even more difficult when Enzo Fernandez was sent off in second-half stoppage time after receiving his second yellow card. Fernandez was carded for a reckless play that sent Spain defender Pau Cubarsi cartwheeling into the air, forcing Argentina to finish the match with only 10 players. About two minutes after play resumed, another foul gave Lamine Yamal a chance to seal the victory from about 22 yards out on a free kick.

 His curling strike toward the right post was saved by Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez, who made a diving stop for his 10th save of the afternoon, the most ever recorded in a World Cup final. Martinez leaped to his feet afterward, punching the air and encouraging the crowd to get loud before the match eventually went to extra time.

 With the victory, Spain became the first nation to simultaneously hold the World Cup crowns in both men's and women's soccer. The final was the 104th and last match of the expanded 48-team tournament played across the United States, Canada and Mexico. Because there were more matches than any previous World Cup, the tournament produced 308 total goals, more than any other edition in history. According to FIFA, the 2026 World Cup was officially the most attended ever.

cards.headline: Flip City Gym and Cheer gymnasts earn top 15 national finish, qualify for Junior Olympics
cards.teaser: Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Sk
cards.body:
Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine represented the gym at the national competition and will advance to compete at the higher level. The trio each discovered gymnastics through unique experiences, with Rose-Daris crediting her ability to do a cartwheel, Supan finding inspiration from watching gymnasts on YouTube, and Rine enjoying the opportunity to continuously learn new skills.

 Head Coach Candice Lazuka praised the team's performance throughout the season, noting they competed at local meets before advancing through states and regionals to reach nationals. At the AAU Nationals competition in Knoxville, the team delivered an exceptional performance that nearly achieved a perfect score. Lazuka explained that earning a perfect 10 is extremely difficult, but the gymnasts managed to score a 9.9, coming very close to perfection. The strong showing at nationals secured their qualification for the Junior Olympics.

 The three gymnasts expressed excitement about the upcoming opportunity to compete at the Junior Olympics in Iowa. Rose-Daris said it's going to be really fun that she's going to an entire different part of the world. Supan described her feelings about the achievement, saying it's happy and exciting at the same time. The young athletes are preparing to take on competitors from across the country at the prestigious event.

 Looking ahead to the Junior Olympics competition, the gymnasts are setting their goals and focusing on specific events. When asked what she is focused on heading into the Junior Olympics, Rine said getting first place on floors. The qualification represents a significant achievement for both the individual gymnasts and Flip City Gym and Cheer as a whole.

 The team's progression from local competitions through the state and regional levels to nationals, and now to the Junior Olympics, demonstrates the dedication and skill development that Lazuka has cultivated in her athletes. The upcoming competition in Iowa will provide Rose-Daris, Supan, and Rine the chance to test themselves against the nation's top junior gymnasts.

cards.headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bobby Portis Jr. join Miami Heat in major trade
cards.teaser: The Miami Heat introduced two-time NBA MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo and forward Bobby Portis Jr. at the Kaseya Center on Thursday, with both players receiving standing ovations from fans.
cards.body:
Thursday afternoon, loud chants of "Giannis" filled the Kaseya Center as the Miami Heat introduced their latest acquisitions. Heat Head Coach Erik Spoelstra said Pat Riley asked him if he wanted to coach Giannis Antetokounmpo, and he said yes. The move brings a two-time MVP, NBA champion, and Finals MVP to South Florida, though questions remain about whether the Heat gave up too much for the star coming off back-to-back injury-filled seasons.

 Antetokounmpo, who stands 6'11 and weighs 240 pounds, told reporters he thrives on pressure and needs it at this point in his career to go to the next level and get out of his comfort zone. He said he was not there to talk about measurables but rather how many championships he can help bring to Miami. Antetokounmpo said he feels like whenever he puts his mind to something, he usually accomplishes it, and this is the best route for him to win more titles.

 The Heat also introduced forward Bobby Portis Jr., who said he prides himself on working every day in the summer to get better and has been coming off the bench his whole career as a sixth man type of guy. Portis said being aggressive is what he has always been about, a mindset that Riley and Spoelstra believe embodies the Miami Heat way of playing basketball.

 Portis, who has been playing with Antetokounmpo for six years, said his relationship with Bam Adebayo has been built off being competitors. Spoelstra said the squad featuring Antetokounmpo, Portis, and Adebayo will play a lot of positionless basketball. Antetokounmpo told reporters he wants to be coached hard so everyone else will follow, adding he does not want feedback sugar-coated and needs the truth so he can apply it to his game.

hero.headline: Boca Raton TLC Program Offers Summer Service Projects for South Florida Families
hero.teaser: B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program connects volunteers with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking and literacy efforts.
hero.body:
B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program is offering South Florida families a range of hands-on service projects this summer, from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors. Led by Summer Faerman, the program connects volunteers of all ages with mitzvah opportunities, or meaningful good deeds, as part of the congregation's broader community outreach efforts.

 The TLC Program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed, and has made service a central part of synagogue life since 2012. The program provides a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida. It addresses multiple community concerns including hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations and special needs. Organizers emphasize that the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation, with the goal of making service practical, welcoming and easy to begin.

 Participants can volunteer in various ways throughout the summer. Projects include making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology. Organizers plan to demonstrate volunteer projects such as wrapping presents, making flower arrangements, preparing sandwiches, collecting shoes and assembling supplies for people in need. The variety of options allows families to choose activities that match their interests and schedules.

 As summer continues, the TLC Program offers families a way to stay connected, teach children about giving back and support neighbors throughout South Florida. B'nai Torah Congregation says the program is built around the idea that small acts of service can strengthen the larger community. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Food Bank serves 2,500 hot meals daily to children at 35 summer sites
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Food Bank in Lake Worth Beach is serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children through Florida's Summer BreakSpot program while school is out.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Food Bank is serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children through Florida's Summer BreakSpot program, according to Food Bank leaders. The nonprofit organization supports more than 35 Summer BreakSpot sites across Palm Beach County while school is out for the summer. During a live Shining A Light broadcast on WPTV, CEO Jamie Kendall and Culinary Director Chef Doug Barg gave viewers a behind-the-scenes look inside the Michelle Hagerty Community Kitchen, where meals are prepared and loaded onto trucks for early morning deliveries across the county.

 The organization prepared more than 36,000 hot meals in June alone. According to the Palm Beach County Food Bank, hunger doesn't take a summer break, highlighting the need for continued support during the summer months. The Summer BreakSpot program provides free meals to children and teens 18 and younger during the summer when school cafeterias are closed. Food Bank leaders said the meals are distributed through partner locations across Palm Beach County to help families facing food insecurity during the summer. Kendall said the Food Bank's partnership with Summer BreakSpot helps ensure children continue receiving nutritious meals while school is out.

 During the broadcast, viewers got a close look at the large-scale kitchen operation responsible for preparing meals daily. Chef Barg walked viewers through the food production process, showing how culinary teams prepare, package and organize meals before they are loaded onto delivery trucks. The loading dock operation featured drivers and volunteers preparing for morning deliveries to Summer BreakSpot sites throughout Palm Beach County. The Palm Beach County Food Bank said volunteers and community support are critical to maintaining the program during the busy summer season.

 The Palm Beach County Food Bank is located at 701 Boutwell Road, Suite A-1, in Lake Worth Beach. Food Bank leaders said the organization continues seeking volunteers, donations and community partnerships to support its mission of reducing childhood hunger in Palm Beach County. Families looking for Summer BreakSpot meal locations can find participating sites throughout the county during the summer months.

cards.headline: Downtown Delray Beach launches Wellness Pass with free fitness classes and spa deals for July and August
cards.teaser: The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority launched the Downtown Delray Wellness Pass for July and August. The mobile-exclusive pass allows users to access complimentary classes, discounted wellness treatments and promotions from participating businesses.
cards.body:
Downtown Delray Beach is encouraging residents and visitors to prioritize health and self-care this summer through a new Wellness Pass featuring free fitness classes, yoga sessions, spa discounts and wellness-focused offers across the city's downtown district. The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority launched the Downtown Delray Wellness Pass for July and August.

 According to the DDA, the mobile-exclusive pass allows users to access complimentary classes, discounted wellness treatments and promotions from participating businesses throughout Downtown Delray Beach. The pass does not require an app download. Miller Physical Therapy is also participating with wellness-related services and promotions. The program arrives as wellness tourism and fitness-focused experiences continue to grow in popularity across South Florida. Many consumers are seeking affordable ways to stay active, reduce stress and support local businesses during the summer months.

cards.headline: Delray Beach dance studio hosts Bridgerton masquerade gala July 24 for ninth anniversary
cards.teaser: Fred Astaire Dance Studios Delray Beach is celebrating nine years with a Bridgerton-style masquerade gala featuring themed decor and dancing.
cards.body:
Fred Astaire Dance Studios Delray Beach, located at 247 SE Sixth Ave., is hosting a Bridgerton-style masquerade gala on July 24 to celebrate its ninth anniversary. The studio is owned by world champion dancers Mar Martinez and Clifton Sepulveda and has built a reputation for welcoming dancers of all experience levels, from beginners to competitive performers. The anniversary gala will feature themed décor, dancing and a celebration of the studio's growth over the past nine years.

 The studio is launching a Summer Boot Camp series beginning July 18 and continuing every Saturday through August. According to Fred Astaire Dance Studios Delray Beach, the classes are designed to help participants learn ballroom and Latin dance fundamentals in a fun, supportive environment. Another upcoming event is a DJ Latin Dance Night open to the public on July 31 from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. Martinez and Sepulveda are also preparing to teach a dance class at Florida Atlantic University beginning in August. More information about upcoming events and classes is available at FredAstaireDelrayBeach.com.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Zoo extends Kids Free program through August 10
cards.teaser: Palm Beach Zoo extended its Kids Free promotion through August 10, allowing up to four children ages 3 to 12 to receive free admission with one adult ticket.
cards.body:
Palm Beach Zoo extended its popular Kids Free promotion through Aug. 10, according to zoo officials. Under the program, up to four children ages 3 to 12 receive free admission with the purchase of one adult ticket. Amanda Joiner, the zoo's chief marketing and technology officer, shared the updates during WPTV's "Shining A Light" segment from the zoo Monday morning. Joiner said the extension is designed to help local families enjoy affordable outings during the hottest stretch of summer while still supporting the zoo's conservation mission. Zoo officials emphasized that families still receive the full zoo experience through the promotion, including access to exhibits, shaded walkways and animal encounters. The zoo is also encouraging visitors to stay cool with indoor spaces, shaded pathways and frozen treats available throughout the park.

 The zoo's newest koala joey is officially a boy and now has a name: Bonza. Joiner said that's Aussie slang for "awesome" or "excellent" during the interview. Palm Beach Zoo also announced the return of its Wild Night Out series, an adults-only after-hours experience happening on the last Saturdays of July, August and September. The themed nights include "Paws & Santa Claus" in July, "Tails & Touchdowns" in August and "Decades After Dark" in September. The events will feature live entertainment, themed activities and performances from bands including Whiskey Six and Snapback. Palm Beach Zoo is located at 1301 Summit Blvd.

hero.headline: 85 percent of Florida families spend more than affordability benchmark on childcare, Fed report finds
hero.body:
The cost of childcare has become an affordability crisis for Florida families, with 85.4 percent spending more than the federal benchmark on care, according to a new report from the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta. The study found that from 2020 to 2024, childcare prices increased by 29 percent nationwide, compared with a 22 percent rise in overall prices during the same period.

The Atlanta Fed examined childcare costs in Georgia and Florida and found that childcare expenses now often far exceed the 7 percent of income affordability benchmark established by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. The estimated weekly costs for the care of infants and toddlers in Florida are $268, while preschool-aged children cost an estimated $208 per week. The median percentage of income families would need to pay for childcare is 13.9 percent.

According to the report, in Florida, the median percentage of income families would need to pay for childcare is 16.8 percent, more than double the federal standard. These costs are putting significant financial pressure on parents across the state and forcing difficult decisions about work hours. Some families are even leaving jobs due to the burden of childcare expenses.

The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta's research highlights a growing economic challenge for working families throughout Florida. The 29 percent increase in childcare prices over four years represents a steeper climb than general inflation, creating a widening gap between what families earn and what they must pay to keep children in care while parents work. The report is available in full from the Atlanta Fed.

cards.headline: Florida back-to-school tax holiday begins, runs through August 20
cards.teaser: Florida families can purchase school supplies, clothing, and electronics without paying sales tax during the month-long tax holiday that started Monday.
cards.body:
Florida's annual back-to-school sales tax holiday kicked off Monday, giving families statewide a chance to save money on school supplies, clothing and electronics ahead of the new school year. The tax-free period runs through Thursday, Aug. 20, allowing shoppers to purchase qualifying items without paying Florida's sales tax. The tax holiday covers clothing, footwear, and accessories priced at $100 or less per item, including shirts, pants, dresses, shoes, boots, and accessories like belts and hats. School supplies under $50 per item are tax-free, covering everything from notebooks and pencils to binders, markers, scissors, and lunch boxes. Learning aids and jigsaw puzzles priced at $30 or less are included, such as flashcards, educational toys, and puzzle books.

Personal computers and related accessories under $1,500 qualify for the tax exemption, including laptops, tablets, desktops, electronic book readers, and accessories like keyboards, mice, monitors, and routers. Cell phones, video game consoles, and recreational devices don't qualify. Wallets and bags under $100 per item are covered, including backpacks, handbags, and fanny packs, though briefcases and suitcases are excluded. The tax holiday doesn't apply to rentals or repairs of qualifying items, and purchases made at theme parks, entertainment complexes, hotels, or airports are excluded from the exemption. Governor Ron DeSantis signed the tax holiday into law as part of the state's effort to help families manage back-to-school expenses.

cards.headline: Donalds holds commanding lead over Collins and Fishback in Florida Republican gubernatorial primary polling
cards.teaser: Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds holds a commanding advantage in polling and fundraising as Florida's August 18 gubernatorial primary approaches, while Democrat David Jolly has consolidated support in his party's contest.
cards.body:
Byron Donalds continues to hold a commanding advantage in Republican polling and fundraising as the August 18 primary approaches. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48 percent, followed by Lt. Gov.

 Jay Collins at 9 percent, businessman James Fishback at 8 percent and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 4 percent. About 26 percent of respondents remained undecided. Donalds also holds a major financial advantage, with his campaign announcing more than $90 million raised across his campaign operation.

 President Donald Trump has endorsed Donalds, while Gov. Ron DeSantis, who appointed Collins lieutenant governor in August 2025, has remained publicly neutral in the primary.

 Collins used a Thursday campaign call to position himself as the strongest Republican alternative to Donalds, despite trailing in polling, money and endorsements. Collins defended his support for Immigration and Customs Enforcement and law enforcement, rejected claims of tension between his campaign and staff inside the governor's office and urged Renner to leave the race.

 Fishback is facing pressure on two fronts. The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, announced a $400,000 campaign targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic.

 Collins is also challenging whether Fishback meets Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee.

cards.headline: Florida's back-to-school tax-free holiday runs through Aug. 20
cards.teaser: Families across the Treasure Coast are shopping during the state's tax-free holiday to save on school supplies, clothing, and electronics before the Aug. 10 start of the school year.
cards.body:
Katrina Stoneking was shopping at Office Depot in Boynton Beach for her soon-to-be 5th grader when she told WPTV she typically spends around $200 or more each year on school supplies. She's hoping the tax-free holiday helps stretch that budget and saves her probably $50 to $60. WPTV priced a random school supply list for a fourth grader in Palm Beach County and the items ring up to about $263.52.

 Thanks to the tax-free holiday, that same cart saves $18.45 in taxes alone. Tameica Petgrave, the general manager of the Boynton Beach Office Depot, said the item parents have been asking about most is 3-ring paper.

 Clothing and accessories priced under $100 each are tax free, including shirts, pants, backpacks, wallets, belts, and graduation caps and gowns. General school supplies priced under $50 each are also exempt, including pens, pencils, and lunch boxes. Electronics like calculators, printers, laptops, and tablets all qualify as long as each item is under $1,500 and purchased for personal use only.

 Items ordered online during the holiday period qualify for the exemption, even if they are delivered after Aug. 20. Notable exclusions include briefcases, suitcases, watches, jewelry, skis, swim fins, rollerblades, and any clothing item over $100. Back-to-school shopping costs parents an average of $922 this year, and 47% of families are expected to pay more than last year, according to a study by PricewaterhouseCoopers.

cards.headline: Man struck and killed fleeing ICE agents in Florida as agency pauses most traffic stops nationwide
cards.teaser: A 28-year-old man died Tuesday after he was struck by a semi trailer truck while fleeing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents near a Florida gas station, prompting ICE to pause most traffic stops nationwide.
cards.body:
A 28-year-old man died in Florida Tuesday after he was struck by a semi trailer truck while attempting to cross State Road 16 near a gas station. The man was fleeing from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, according to state officials. He was one of four people who fled the scene. Florida Highway Patrol officials confirmed they were not involved in the incident but have since opened an investigation into the death.

 In a statement to Scripps News, the state highway patrol said an encounter between HSI and ICE agents occurred in the parking lot of a local gas station. During the encounter, the four occupants of the vehicle fled on foot. One of the occupants ran across State Road 16 and into the path of the tractor trailer.

 The pedestrian was struck by the tractor trailer in the right lane and sustained fatal injuries on scene. The death comes as ICE is under increasing scrutiny for multiple fatal encounters. Joan Sebastian Guerrero, a 26-year-old Colombian man living in Maine, was fatally shot by ICE agents Monday during a traffic stop.

 Days earlier, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was fatally wounded during a traffic stop involving ICE in Houston. Like the shooting in Maine, Salgado Araujo was not the person ICE was trying to find. The Trump administration ordered Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents to pause most traffic stops on Tuesday.

cards.headline: Security First Insurance lowers Florida homeowners rates by average of 5.6 percent, launches disappearing deductible program
cards.teaser: Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6 percent, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years as state reforms reduce lawsuits.
cards.body:
Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6 percent, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years. Melissa Burt DeVriese, president of Security First, said customers are seeing the impact of the rate decreases. Insurance companies have been reducing rates or holding them stable as more companies cite a reduction in lawsuits from state reforms. Burt DeVriese said all those savings are required to be passed along to customers, and the company has been doing so.

 Security First also announced new discounts and a disappearing deductible that rewards claims-free customers by reducing their deductible over time. Over the course of five years, every year the deductible goes down 20 percent as long as there is no loss. Once a loss occurs, the discounted deductible applies, and then it resets back to the full deductible amount.

 Based in Ormond Beach, Security First has about 155,000 policies in the state. Burt DeVriese said Security First is committed to writing more policies in southeast Florida. Online firm Insurify reports that in 2026 Florida homeowners pay the highest average premium in the country at $8,292. State insurance regulators said that with more companies and more competition, homeowners should seek better premiums by shopping around.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth backs low-altitude military flyovers after Blue Angels jet buzzes Pensacola beach
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth defended low-altitude military flyovers after a Blue Angels jet flew so low over a crowded Pensacola beach Wednesday that chairs and tents went flying and sand kicked up, prompting a Navy safety review that was quickly curtailed.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth wrote on his personal X account Thursday that military flyovers will continue after a Blue Angels jet flew so low over a crowded Pensacola beach Wednesday that chairs and tents went flying, sand kicked up and children held their hands over their ears, according to video spreading widely on social media. The U.S. Navy said in a statement shortly afterward that it was conducting a thorough safety review.

 Then on Thursday morning, Trump administration officials heaped praise on the maneuver. Hegseth wrote that the flyovers will continue until morale improves, without elaborating. The Pentagon's top spokesman, Sean Parnell, wrote Carry on Patriots on social media alongside a photo showing a Blue Angels jet with a wingtip just feet above the heads of beachgoers. The White House tweeted a cartoon showing people on a beach taking photos of a Blue Angels jet, with the words Freedom and It's okay to love America.

 Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said the Navy had no problem with the flight and there would be no reprimands or firings. His social media post was retweeted by Hegseth. Cao's post said Thursday that the Blue Angels conducted a flight debrief.

 Navy officials would not say if that debrief was the thorough safety review the Navy said it would conduct the day prior. This marks at least the third time that Hegseth and others have voiced support for military aviators performing maneuvers that have drawn public scrutiny and military investigations. In two prior cases, Hegseth's remarks led to the end of safety investigations.

 Aviation safety consultant Jeff Guzzetti, who used to investigate crashes for the National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration, said flyovers at low altitudes like these have been linked to past crashes. A Navy official said the Blue Angels' next show on Saturday will go on as scheduled.

hero.headline: Martin County deputies rescue 80 cats from Stuart home in worst hoarding case sheriff has seen
hero.body:
Martin County deputies rescued dozens of cats Monday from a Stuart home that Sheriff John Budensiek described as the worst animal hoarding case he has seen in the county. The Martin County Sheriff's Office, Animal Control and Martin County Fire Rescue responded to a home in the 11500 block of Southwest Meadowlark Circle after an investigation into reports that a U.S. Postal Service employee had been collecting feral cats along her mail route.

Budensiek identified the homeowner as 77-year-old Gail Giustino. Investigators believe she was not stealing pets but was gathering feral cats and bringing them home. Authorities obtained a search warrant after Giustino allegedly refused to allow Animal Control officers inside the home during multiple attempts over the past week. When deputies entered the house Monday, they found what the sheriff described as horrific living conditions. The home had no working air conditioning, little to no ventilation and, in some areas, up to a foot of animal feces covering the floor. Budensiek said the odor was overwhelming, and Martin County Fire Rescue's Hazardous Materials Team had to ventilate the home before rescuers could safely enter.

Giustino told deputies she believed there were at least 70 cats inside the home, all kept in cages. Authorities believe there could ultimately be 70 to 80 animals or more, including several dogs, though an exact count had not been completed Monday evening. The rescued animals are being taken to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, which is expected to rely on foster families and volunteers to help care for them. Authorities said they are still evaluating the animals' medical conditions. Officials said Animal Control had previously cited Giustino dozens of times for animal-related violations about 10 years ago, but they believe she gradually returned to hoarding animals after complying with earlier code enforcement requirements.

Budensiek said Giustino was arrested on two misdemeanor animal cruelty-related charges, though investigators said they could have pursued significantly more charges. The sheriff said the criminal charges were filed primarily to obtain the search warrant, remove the animals from the home and prevent Giustino from acquiring additional animals while she seeks help through the mental health court system. "If we believe she was truly an animal abuser ... we would try to bury her under the jail," Budensiek said. "We truly believe that Gail thinks she's doing the right thing, but she's doing it the wrong way."

cards.headline: Hobe Sound couple seeks community support as husband battles head and neck cancer
cards.teaser: A Hobe Sound couple is asking for community support as they navigate a cancer diagnosis, holding onto faith every step of the way.
cards.body:
Dave and Faren Motz met in South Florida before moving to Maui, where they married and raised their family. Faren raised all three of their kids and home schooled. The couple started a business and had a farm where they served children.

 Years later, they moved to Hobe Sound and purchased a property, but just months after settling in, Dave was diagnosed with head and neck cancer. As the couple searched for the right healthcare in Florida, AdventHealth in Celebration provided programs and grants that became a critical resource.

 Dave underwent nearly seven weeks of daily radiation treatments. The repeated visits to Orlando, biopsies, scans, and exams added up, costing the couple nearly $20,000 out of pocket. Their age and income kept them from qualifying for Medicare or Medicaid.

 Dave, a former firefighter, had long been the family's provider. Now, Faren has stepped up to support them both, driving him back and forth from Orlando for treatment. Doctors told Dave he has an 85% chance of recovery.

 Faren works at Latitudes at the Jupiter Beach Resort, where those who want to show their support can stop by and visit. Those who would like to contribute financially can donate to the family's GoFundMe at Standing with Dave Motz in his cancer battle.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County man arrested after leading Martin County deputies on 100 mph chase through Indiantown
cards.teaser: A 33-year-old man led Martin County deputies on a high-speed chase through Indiantown after driving more than 100 mph on State Road 710.
cards.body:
Deputies spotted 33-year-old Markell Tillman driving aggressively at speeds exceeding 100 mph on State Road 710, forcing other vehicles off the roadway. When deputies attempted to stop him, Tillman fled. Tillman weaved through traffic in an attempt to lose deputies before turning onto SW Martin Highway toward Palm City, where he continued to drive recklessly.

 Deputies spotted Tillman again traveling eastbound on Martin Highway near Allapattah Road. Deputies used stop sticks to disable his vehicle near I-95. Tillman then bailed out of the vehicle and attempted to flee on foot before deputies caught up with him and took him into custody.

 Tillman was arrested on charges including fleeing and eluding, aggravated fleeing with injury or damage, operating a vehicle exceeding the speed limit by 50 or more mph, driving while license suspended or revoked, obstruction without violence, and operating a vehicle at 100 or more mph. Tillman also had an out-of-county warrant at the time of his arrest. He was booked into the Martin County Jail.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.teaser: Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton.
cards.body:
Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized.

 The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay. Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete.

 Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, said Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab. With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine, the district was able to add these on.

 The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out. The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027.
